name: tephra
description: Redraw any image as black-background pixel art in one of two canonical modes: moving stroke particles for fluids, or a static ordered-dither solid that can be combed into hard-edged fracture streaks for figures. Physics-planned regional motion, seamless loops.

interface.shortDescription: Two-mode pixel redraws: stroke particles or dithered solids
interface.longDescription: A deterministic renderer that redraws an image on pure black in one of two canonical modes, chosen by subject. PURE PARTICLE: short strokes follow the image's own structure-tensor direction field and really travel along it -- right for waves, smoke, light shafts, anything already in motion. DITHERED SOLID: the image's tone becomes an ordered 8x8 dither that stays perfectly still frame to frame, and can be combed along a direction into hard-edged fracture streaks -- right for figures, sculpture, animals, architecture, where contour and volume have to read. Per-region motion is planned from the picture's physics, density conservation removes field-attractor artifacts, and every animation loops seamlessly. Outputs PNG, GIF and MP4.
defaultPrompt: Redraw this image as flowing pixel-particle art with a seamless loop.
Turn this picture into black-background particle strokes that move along its structure.
Make an animated tephra version of this image for a video cover.
